The helper source at presentation_attract_overlay_impl computes the desired actor phase, compares it with PRES_ACTOR_PHASE, then writes the new phase and calls PRES_MAIN_FB_PREPARE before copying actors. Bounded A1 hypothesis and proposed one-file delta

Hypothesis: if the desired actor phase differs while PENDING is set, the overlay should preserve the old PRES_ACTOR_PHASE and return before beginning another BACK transaction. The next normal Attract dispatch can recompute the phase and admit it after PENDING clears. This avoids advancing the phase cache before admission. It neither clears PENDING nor waits in a loop, and it does not guarantee a visible repair or replay every intermediate phase.

The only proposed production file is the fresh candidate's src/perimeter_reset_helper.s. Insert direct-page `tst PENDING` and short `bne pao_done` on the phase-change path, before `sta PRES_ACTOR_PHASE` and before `jsr PRES_MAIN_FB_PREPARE`. Use the existing same-helper PENDING admission style. Keep the actor copy and finish/capture path unchanged. No change has been applied yet.

The helper allocation is $06B2-$07FF inclusive (334 bytes; exclusive end $0800). The current image occupies [$06B2,$07FD), 331 bytes; it leaves three bytes at $07FD-$07FF. The proposed TST and BNE cost four bytes. Recover exactly one byte by changing `lbsr presentation_attract_phase` at $0786 to `bsr presentation_attract_phase`. Current bytes are 17 00 5B and target $07E4. After both edits, the callee moves to $07E7 and the BSR return address is $0788, giving projected signed displacement +95 ($5F), within the 6809 BSR range -128..+127. Projected BSR bytes are 8D 5F. The guard at $078C is projected as 0D 91 26 53: direct TST of PENDING=$91, then BNE from $0790 to pao_done at $07E3. The phase store moves to $0790 and the prepare JSR to $0792. Net growth is three bytes; projected helper size is exactly 334/334 and its exclusive end is $0800. The listing and compiled bytes must confirm every address and displacement; these are not yet built facts.

BSR and LBSR are both relative subroutine calls and both push a return address for RTS. A compiled postcheck must decode the actual BSR target and return path, not assume the target stayed at $07E4. The BNE destination must decode to pao_done. The helper has zero spare bytes after the proposed change. Any source drift, different instruction width, changed target, branch out of range, or size other than 334 stops the step. Do not widen the allocation, relocate unrelated code, or edit the full presentation runtime, which is already 1,280/1,280 bytes.

The prior no-input run observed a pending interval at the actor boundary, not its producer, commit, visible frame, or rollback. The A1 actor-admission guard does not change menu ordering or prove A2 behavior.

Source-only findings

In `src/shared_text_stage.inc`, `highscore_attract_tick` calls `highscore_logo_tick` before `menu_tick` (lines 1306–1311). The logo path checks PENDING and may prepare/finish a redraw. `menu_tick` can then change MENU_SELECT and set MENU_DIRTY; `menu_idle` defers its painter when PENDING is set. In `src/presentation_runtime.s`, Attract calls the page-23 callback before the actor overlay. The actor overlay stores a changed phase and calls prepare without checking PENDING. `framebuffer_prepare_back` checks initialization and BACK/FRONT ownership but not PENDING; `framebuffer_finish_back` captures and sets PENDING. This is a credible shared publication-delay candidate. It does not identify a runtime producer or prove a visible rollback.

A separate clock candidate is source-supported: `attract_tick` increments PRES_TIMER; an Attract MENU_EVENT clears it; `presentation_attract_phase` derives actor phase from PRES_TIMER. This may restart actor animation during navigation, independently of whether menu painting is deferred. No input run has established the reported stutter. MENU_SELECT also clears on `menu_change`, so an exact screen/input sequence is needed to distinguish an expected screen transition from a logical reversal.

A1 guard boundary

The approved A1 check defers actor phase storage and prepare while PENDING is set. It does not reorder logo and menu callbacks, change menu edge/selection/dirty state, prevent the Attract timer reset, or prove FRONT pixels. It cannot close A2 coverage.

User prioritizes navigation-induced animation reset before the unresolved no-input stutter and requests design/code impacts. Confirmed path: presentation_runtime.s attract_tick increments PRES_TIMER, calls the page-$23 title/menu callback, then checks idle expiry and calls the actor overlay. shared_text_stage.inc clears both PRES_TIMER bytes after an Attract menu event. perimeter_reset_helper.s computes the actor phase from PRES_TIMER minus6, with three shifts and a two-bit mask; phase3 displays frame1. Thus the existing menu event resets the input to the actor phase calculation. PRES_ACTOR_PHASE is a render cache, not an independent elapsed clock; merely retaining that byte cannot preserve subsequent phase timing. The logo already uses a separate IRQ-atomic VBLANK clock and its reserved three-byte slot is occupied.

Preferred design for evaluation: retain PRES_TIMER as the continuous Attract animation timebase, and store a separate16-bit last-activity timestamp. At navigation, copy PRES_TIMER into that timestamp rather than clearing PRES_TIMER. Before idle comparison, subtract the timestamp from PRES_TIMER using unsigned16-bit arithmetic and retain the existing558-count threshold. Initialize the timestamp at every natural/wake/re-entry Attract boundary. No second per-tick counter or new timing source is needed. The menu handler must preserve its loaded MENU_EVENT in A while recording the timestamp: LDD clobbers A/B, so a naive LDD/STD replacement is incorrect. Luna Extra High independently confirms LDX PRES_TIMER / STX idle_origin is the smaller candidate because it preserves A; prove X is disposable along every subsequent event path before selecting it. Exact local instruction selection remains a fit task.

Code/allocation impact: projected production scope is presentation_runtime.s (initialization and idle comparison) and shared_text_stage.inc (timestamp capture/state alias). Leave the full334-byte actor helper unchanged if this design remains viable. Both modules need one consistent documented state address. Two bytes of persistent state are required; an existing demo/name-only alias is a candidate only after all lifetimes/readers/writers and re-entry initialization are proved. Luna review excludes E8/E9 because the active logo path uses them, excludes the occupied A8FD-A8FF logo slot, and does not qualify B2 gameplay input history as spare. No state address is approved here. Under DP=$00, one extra direct SUBD costs2 code bytes; two direct CLRs for initialization cost4. Those6 bytes are a lower-bound local projection, not total assembled growth: event preservation, repeated entry sites, conditional profiles and branch ranges can add code. Presentation is already1280/1280, so even this lower bound needs local recovery or a revised placement. Resident104 bytes free cannot directly fill a different fixed module without an approved call-boundary change.

2. Exact change and recommended design

Contract replacement: command_id identifies the API request; a unique native MI token identifies its command result/error. An asynchronous stop is instead an owner/session/generation/event-sequence observation, with preserved raw fields and attribution=SESSION_EVENT_ONLY. Do not populate cause_command_id or imply that delivery after a result proves the command caused the stop. Native signal/breakpoint predicates remain strict; absent signal stays UNKNOWN. A second token-correlated state query must confirm that the target is currently stopped at the expected thread/PC, with no intervening state-generation change. That confirms a snapshot, not historical causation or a signal reconstructed from a query.

Fresh opt-in observation mode: after normal owned startup completes, add claim_observed_session(owner_id,session_id,budget_ms). It may claim only a fresh ACTIVE lease with completed startup, no user-command/interrupt history, no pending legacy reader and no closing/taint. Add explicit stdout-ownership and post-ACTIVE user/interrupt-history fields; the generic pending-task set is not sufficient evidence of reader ownership. Claim-pending ownership is registered synchronously before the first await, so racing legacy calls reject before writing. Fully awaited startup reaches ACTIVE only after its original banner/setup reads have completed. Repeating the identical claim returns the same generation/reader; changed owner or reused/nonfresh session rejects. Reader adoption of an arbitrary existing session and reconnect are excluded.

Claim transfers stdout to exactly one persistent owned reader and a separate tokenized command-result dispatcher, not the old command-local reader. Begin journaling before issuing the baseline query; buffered startup output is retained as pre-fence/unknown history, not retroactively attributed. A record delivered after the fence is not proof that the physical event happened after it. It preserves bounded raw records, assigns increasing event sequence and tracks UNKNOWN/STOPPED/RUNNING/CLOSING/TAINTED state without treating prompts as proof of a stop. Only token-matched native command results complete requests. A stop seen before an observation fence is ineligible for a later phase; multiple/contradictory/unexpected state changes, MI errors or unsupported records prevent acceptance. A delayed event that is indistinguishable from a current event is still only an observation; no fixture may pretend its cause is known.

For claimed sessions, legacy send and direct interrupt must reject before writing or signaling. Record preclaim user/interrupt use so a previously used session cannot appear fresh. Unclaimed legacy sessions retain their existing APIs and behavior. Default startup/spawn/launch arguments, lease registration, late-handle ownership and process wait/TERM/KILL rules remain unchanged. Do not rewrite the legacy reader or migrate ordinary sessions to the new mode. The completed startup reader must have returned and its tasks be terminal before claim; the new reader begins in UNKNOWN, and a fixed tokenized baseline query must establish no attached target before this fresh session is admitted for its initial attach. Unexpected residual stops or an already attached/running target reject claim. Startup is not retroactively claimed as journaled evidence. Claim failure after reader handoff retains observer ownership and requires observed-stop cleanup; never revert that session to a second legacy reader. Empty thread output alone must not be treated as proof of no attachment if native target state remains ambiguous; unavailable baseline proof is UNKNOWN and held for native reassessment.

Implement exec_owned_session on the claimed mode: owner/session validation, single-use command identity, native result token, raw MI result/error, raw stop observation, sequence/generation and separately token-matched current-state query. Preserve optional async tokens but never use them as a universal causation guarantee. The current-state query is fixed and read-only, initially -thread-info; require stopped state and a usable frame PC for the single CoCo target thread. Missing/unsupported native fields yield UNKNOWN, not a console-text fallback. Before each continuation, also use a fixed tokenized -break-list query to validate the intended enabled breakpoint number/address and temporary disposition. After the observed stop, match its native breakpoint identity/frame and fresh thread PC to that pre-resume record. Temporary breakpoints may already have been deleted after their hit; do not require a temporary breakpoint to remain enabled afterward. The GNU breakpoint command reference documents these query fields and temporary insertion. If a fixed query cannot support the required native proof, stop for a separate proposal; no native attempt is authorized here.

Add stop_observed_session(owner_id,budget_ms) to invalidate observations before shutdown and report process_exit_confirmed and reader_exit_confirmed separately. Reuse stop-by-owner/direct wait under one enclosing deadline; never reset a timeout for the reader join. Existing emergency process-stop paths stay available and invalidate active observation admission. Process EXITED alone is not reader cleanup. Keep an owner-addressable observer/task reference until it terminates; if the process exits but the reader does not, report cleanup_complete=false and retain UNRESOLVED observer ownership. No silent task detachment, registry loss or cancellation-as-exit proof.

Target and bounded design

File target: introduce a JSON raw-byte maximum of16777216bytes (16MiB;1MiB=1048576bytes), retain the existing16777216 .NET UTF-16-code-unit JSON character maximum, and read in chunks of at most4096bytes. The byte bound is new and can reject documents previously within the character bound; it is not a cap increase. Current freeze is47582bytes, a single observed baseline; no maximum receipt size or execution cost is claimed. No total-process RSS limit is promised.

Check available stream length only as an early rejection, never as the sole bound. The actual accumulation loop requests no more than the remaining allowance plus one detection byte, retains at most the byte maximum, stops at the first over-limit byte, and decodes only after bounded EOF. Invalid encoding fails, without replacement characters. 2026-10-25 - Proposed scope amendment: HUD alignment and full credit retirement

Disposition: High-risk feature, Proposed; renewed user approval is required before implementation. This material amendment returns FEAT-010 to Proposed. The existing 2026-10-14 approval deferred gameplay credit handling and HUD credit labels. The user now requests a consistent right HUD based on tiled/coco-template.tmx, removal of all credit logic, and updated PART/current-score/top-score writers. The user clarified that all credit logic is to be removed. This amendment does not authorize source edits, builds, or runtime work.

Objective and motivation: make the template the single authored reference for the right-side HUD, align every other Tiled screen that carries that HUD, retire the obsolete credit feature throughout the running game, and make dynamic PART, 1ST/current-score, and TOP/high-score values land at the template's intended cells. This also removes the legacy Coin Positions build requirement. At source revision be911f1e, DOC-015 records the current full build stopping because scripts/build_presentation.py still requires that intentionally deprecated layer. No current combined artifact or capacity result qualifies this amendment.

Golden path: cold start publishes the approved Attract screen; selecting Start begins play with no credit check or debit; gameplay shows the template-aligned PART, current score, and TOP score; normal score/high-score and part updates remain visible at their new destinations; level-start, extra, special, game-over, name-entry, and ranking handoffs keep the same HUD alignment where the authored screen carries the side HUD. No cabinet-credit counter, paid-play prompt, credit-only sound, or free-play award appears or changes state. Live gameplay pickups and their existing score/reward effects remain unchanged. The informational Credits/About page remains available under the previously approved menu flow.

In scope:

  • Use the current tiled/coco-template.tmx right-HUD layout as the authored target. Align the HUD fields in tiled/coco-screen.tmx, tiled/coco-enter-high-score-screen.tmx, tiled/coco-extra-screen.tmx, tiled/coco-game-over-screen.tmx, tiled/coco-instructions-screen.tmx, tiled/coco-level-start-screen.tmx, and tiled/coco-special-screen.tmx. Remove CREDIT label/tile data and obsolete coin-position metadata. Preserve each map's non-HUD content and the left-side SPECIAL/EXTRA/multiplier HUD.
  • Retire production credit state and behavior, including the PRES_CREDITS counter, coin input edges on physical 5/6, credit-based admission/debit or awards, coin-slot drawing, credit-only audio queue/service, and credit-specific render bookkeeping. Physical 5/6 must have no credit effect. Preserve free Start and all unrelated gameplay score, life, EXTRA, SPECIAL score, and informational Credits/About behavior.
  • Update the PART, active 1ST/current-score, and TOP/high-score dynamic writers to the target cells shown by the template across gameplay and presentation owners. Preserve existing score arithmetic, high-score record capacity, ranking semantics, and PART progression. Keep the approved PART format: fixed tens/units cells, hundreds immediately left for values 100-255, and a blank hundreds cell below 100.
  • Remove the generator's Coin Positions dependency and update only existing build guards/verifiers whose accepted contract explicitly depends on retired credit data or behavior. Preserve the normal build workflow and existing hard limits.

Expected affected artifacts for the eventual Ready assignment: the seven named HUD maps and canonical template; scripts/build_presentation.py and directly affected existing map/text verifiers; src/main.s, src/presentation_runtime.s, src/keybinding_runtime.s, src/audio_runtime.s, src/adaptive_audio_bindings.s, src/adaptive_audio_service.s, src/adaptive_active.s, src/demo_runtime.s, src/shared_text_runtime.inc, src/shared_text_stage.inc, and src/shared_text_ranking.inc where the current owner is confirmed. No RNG, clock, framebuffer history, guest RAM writes, or host input. Command: from repository root, python3 scripts/verify_bug016_presentation_layers.py --tiled-dir tiled. The existing verifier is to compare each named HUD label's cells against the template using an independent TMX/XML cell oracle and confirm non-HUD/left-HUD cells are unchanged. One attempt, 60-second whole-phase maximum; callback cap not applicable; measured cost unknown until qualification. Retain command output, manifest hash, and the two mutant rejection results. Approved acceptance cards

  1. NO-CREDIT-FLOW — informational Credits/About, ignored cabinet-credit keys, and free Start; manual natural-path card. Distinct risk: deleting the paid-play system could break the preserved information page or ordinary game start. Owner: user; no agent monitoring. Artifact: final keyboard/adaptive complete-profile 64 KiB GMC candidate, with its post-build ROM SHA-256 recorded before the session. Setup: cold start XRoar with xroar -machine coco3 -machine-cpu 6809 -ram 512 -ram-init random -cart-type gmc -cart-rom build/ladybug.rom -cart-autorun -tv-input rgb -joy-right "" -joy-left ""; no guest-memory writes, injected breakpoints, or special controller. Procedure: view Attract; visit Credits/About and return; press/release physical 5 once and 6 once; then press Return once. Expected: Credits/About retains its information and returns normally; 5/6 do not create a credit, prompt, display change, or credit sound; Return starts a game with no credit prerequisite. Negative control: Return must produce the expected visible start after 5/6 were ignored, proving that keyboard input and the game are responsive. Tolerance: exact transitions and no credit response; no timing target. Deadline: no fixed maximum by explicit FEAT-010 manual-test exception; the user may stop or resume, and incomplete observations remain pending. Retain ROM hash, emulator settings/version if available, and a short result per step. Setup failure, product mismatch, and unobserved step are reported separately.
  2. HUD-VALUES — credit display removal, PART formatting, score/TOP placement, and natural replay; manual visual card. Distinct risk: removing credit drawing or moving shared score writers could erase or shift unrelated HUD fields. Owner: user, using the same final keyboard/adaptive complete-profile ROM; continue the prior cold-start session where practical. Procedure: during ordinary play and natural screen returns, confirm no CREDIT label/count or “ADD CREDITS” remains; inspect current score, TOP, PART, vegetable/bonus, and life fields against the frozen tiled/coco-template.tmx layout. Record the visible PART representations at 99 ( 99), 100 (100), and 255 (255), and confirm the current-score field can pass TOP without shifting the ranking or neighboring labels. No cheat menu, forced RAM state, or pixel-capture controller is used. Independent expected result: the pinned template and the explicit values above. Negative control: while score changes during normal play, the current-score value must change in its own field while static labels, PART, and neighboring fields stay in place; after a screen return, the same fields must still be legible. Tolerance: exact displayed digits and no clipping/overlap; no exact pixel-history claim. Deadline: no fixed manual-session cap; user may stop at any time. A value not naturally reached is reported as missing coverage, not pass or product failure. Retain ROM hash and a checklist of each observed value/transition.
  3. PICKUP-RETENTION — ordinary collection remains active; representative natural gameplay card. Distinct risk: broad credit cleanup could remove a gameplay collection/reward path. Owner: user; continue from free Start without memory writes. Collect one ordinary flower during normal play. Expected: the flower disappears, its collected count changes once, and score increases by the documented 10 points. Negative control: a neighboring uncollected flower remains and does not change the score until separately collected. This is a representative manual check, not exhaustive coverage of all 117 cells or all item types; source review protects the remaining collection paths. The SPECIAL intermission coin/reward is checked only by FEAT-011 IS-03 and is not duplicated here. Deadline: no fixed cap; user may stop, and an unobserved pickup remains pending. Retain ROM hash and observed before/after score and item state.
  4. PROFILE-FIT — three supported complete-profile builds and candidate capacity; automated build/capacity gate. Distinct risk: a profile-specific omission or cumulative integration can break the 64 KiB GMC image or fixed memory limits. Owner: parent integration after Ready. Use the frozen FEAT-010-only candidate repro/feat010-only-candidate-20261031-r3/. It has three separate profile copies and output roots. Use the exact identity-guarded commands in profile-commands.txt, once per profile in the listed order. They replace the earlier example paths and command text while preserving the approved profiles, order, and time bounds. Before dispatch, confirm timeout --version identifies GNU coreutils. Each supervisor sends TERM at 595 seconds and allows at most five seconds before KILL, bounding that whole build command at 600 seconds. Stop after the first nonzero result; do not retry. There is no fourth combined or repeatability build because the removed command duplicated keyboard/adaptive settings and inputs. Each ROM must be 65,536 bytes and pass the existing fixed-capacity checks. Report presentation module use against 1,280 bytes and actual resident headroom; do not impose a minimum headroom. After all three builds pass, use the keyboard/adaptive complete-profile tree for the control pair: source inspection shows the verifier's unconditional 1,280-byte guard is shared across complete profiles, and the three distinct builds still cover profile-specific integration. 2026-11-03 — Source diagnosis: Attract menu input is screened out

Finding: The source contains a direct mismatch between the new Attract menu and the existing key-event filter. The frozen keyboard/adaptive candidate assigns Attract screen ID 0, High Score 3, Options 6, and Credits/About 7. The key scanner publishes menu events only for screen ID 3 or IDs at least 6. On Attract ID 0, it branches around the code that updates the menu-event byte at $00D0. The Attract handler waits for that byte before calling the menu logic. A Down or Enter may therefore be sampled but never delivered to the Attract menu. This is the strongest source-based explanation for the reported symptom; it is not a live runtime confirmation.

Why prior keyboard success is compatible: The retained 2026-10-07 beta build record identifies a complete keyboard/adaptive ROM, SHA-256 7a676d149bf2e46771b1341fe90b03479b5d79c5d7ceecef75fda37269d6edce, tested byte-identically to that build. The beta source and current candidate use the same menu-screen filter. The candidate adds Attract-specific menu handling but leaves the filter unchanged. Earlier gameplay or menu keyboard support therefore does not demonstrate that the newly interactive Attract screen is admitted by the filter.

Smallest correction to prepare: extend the scanner's allowed-screen condition to include Attract ID 0, while preserving the existing High Score, Options, and Credits/About cases. Prefer using the shared screen constant if the separately assembled keybinding module can consume it without adding a fragile duplicated value. Keep the frozen candidate unchanged until a fresh candidate is prepared.

Existing-verifier gap: The current presentation-flow verifier checks that Attract reads $00D0 and dispatches to the menu, but it does not check that the key scanner writes an event for Attract screen ID 0. The menu verifier has no assertion for this scanner-to-menu event path. The existing checks therefore cover the receiver but miss the screen filter that blocks the event.

Discriminating debug check: On a revision-identified candidate, stop in the key scanner after the Down row is sampled. On Attract, confirm $00A6=0, the Down sample at $0292 has bit $08, and the current filter skips the menu-event update at $00D0. After the correction, the same input should set menu event bit $02, move selection $00E0 from 0 to 1, mark the menu dirty, and publish the changed highlight. No source patch, build, emulator launch, or runtime check was performed for this diagnosis. The earlier runtime diagnosis remains inconclusive because it stopped before a visible Attract baseline or any game key.

Evidence: candidate key scanner, candidate Attract menu handler, generated screen IDs, and beta build record. FEAT-010 remains In Progress.

2026-11-03 — Proposed amendment: shared High Score painter, visual corrections, and return to Attract

Lifecycle and class: This material change returns FEAT-010 to Proposed, High-risk, and not Ready. The existing approval still governs the earlier free-start, credit-removal, apostrophe, and attract-rotation work. This amendment asks to add one shared High Score ranking painter plus the reported visual and timed-return repairs. It authorizes no implementation, build, test, emulator action, runtime check, commit, or adoption.

Objective: Attract's automatic High Score stop and the post-game High Score stop must use the same ranking painter, layout data, and display timer. The two callers may prepare records differently: Attract reads existing records without changing them; post-game preserves its existing name-entry and one-time record-commit responsibilities, then hands the resulting records to the shared painter.

Baseline: The user's manual result is the keyboard/adaptive ROM candidate 20261103-02, SHA-256 4d3d291d61b2e3351769e2ed359232ad615f6d61facdaa33d9820db2b664c4b6. The user reports that the Attract High Score view has no names or scores; post-game names/scores use old positions and overlap “TODAY'S TOP SCORES”; the animated logo is two cells above its authored logo; lowercase y/g and registered-mark colors are wrong; and neither reported High Score path returns to Attract when its display interval expires. The post-game view also appeared frozen. Earlier candidate reports disagree about whether gameplay life markers and a first-life animation appeared. These are observations, not a new runtime measurement.

Source findings: The frozen candidate and E worktree match for the eight inspected runtime, build, map, and color inputs. The High Score screen is ID 3, below the Options ID in the complete-profile UI dispatcher. presentation_ui_tick sends screens at or above Options to the page-$23 menu handler; High Score instead goes to the low-memory auxiliary runtime. The shared_text_stage.inc menu_tick routine contains a 558-tick High Score timeout, waits for pending frame work to clear, then selects Attract. That timeout is not reached through the ordinary High Score dispatch shown in presentation_runtime.s. This is a confirmed source-path mismatch and a plausible common cause for both reported return failures; no live timer value or transition was observed, so the runtime root cause remains unconfirmed. The Attract/demo and post-game High Score overlay code are separately assembled, which also permits their table rendering to diverge.

Layout and existing display rule: The current builder places the first dynamic name/score on row 2, where the authored title occupies the same cells. The frozen map and generated placement are documented in the source trace. The shared layout must take its placement from the authored High Score Tiled map. Preserve the already approved display-only ranking rule: show the existing nine stored records as TOP and 1ST–9TH, with the highest record in TOP and 1ST and the remaining eight in 2ND–9TH. Do not change ranking policy, record capacity, or game-over commit ownership.

Proposed design: Reuse the current low-RAM overlay approach. Provide one built High Score painter and one layout source that both entry paths call. After the Attract demo, install that painter for the High Score stop and restore the demo overlay before the next demo. The post-game route uses the same painter after its existing record preparation. Use one timer owner for both visible High Score screens: begin the existing 558 presentation-tick interval after the screen is visible, complete any pending framebuffer handoff, then load and publish Attract. Derive all name/score destinations from the authored map rather than maintaining a second coordinate list. Preserve the existing High Score overlay ceiling of 920 bytes in $0300-$0697 and the 1,280-byte presentation-module ceiling; do not raise either limit. The old 32-byte resident-headroom threshold is retired and is not reinstated by this proposal. Exact routine ownership, data handoff, module fit, and frame-publication details are Ready design work.

In scope: one painter and generated layout for both High Score entry routes; correction of the title/record row collision and missing Attract records; alignment of animated logo tiles with the authored logo; correction of the reported lowercase y/g and registered-mark colors from the authored color data; one 558-tick High Score interval and Attract return on both routes; and preventing gameplay simulation or the gameplay first-life entry animation from running while the ranking screen is shown.

Out of scope: right-HUD corrections on other screens, Attract menu selection stutter, gameplay enemy-speed reports, ranking eligibility/order/record ownership changes, a lives counter above 12, and new life-indicator artwork on High Score. Whether the static High Score background should contain life markers remains undecided and is not an acceptance condition. The screen must not start gameplay life-entry animation.

Acceptance and distinct risks: (1) Attract and post-game reach the same built painter and map-derived placements; Attract leaves records unchanged and post-game commits a qualifying record no more than once. This covers separate overlay selection and duplicated layout drift. (2) TOP and all nine ranked rows are visible in authored non-title cells, and “TODAY'S TOP SCORES” remains unobscured. The animated logo aligns with its authored cells, and lowercase y/g plus ® use their authored intended colors, not white. This covers the reported table, logo-position, and color defects. (3) On the Attract-loop High Score route, fresh supported input returns to Attract with Start selected and is consumed. On the post-game High Score route, fresh input also returns to Attract with Start selected and is consumed. Held input must not start a game across either transition. With no input, each route returns to Attract after 558 presentation ticks once pending frame work is clear. Neither route runs gameplay life-entry or simulation while High Score is visible. This covers route initialization, input consumption, timer ownership, dispatch, and framebuffer handoff. (4) The three already approved profile builds—keyboard/adaptive, joystick/adaptive, and keyboard/nonadaptive—pass all existing hard capacity guards, including the 920-byte High Score overlay and 1,280-byte presentation module. This covers cross-profile assembly and memory fit. (5) User-owned manual acceptance on the final keyboard/adaptive ROM observes both natural sequences and the corrected visible table, logo, and colors. This covers integrated screen behavior; the user controls the play session duration.

Dependencies and order: Approval of this amendment → Ready assignment with exact shared data/routine ownership, map-derived layout handoff, timer/framebuffer design, commands and evidence roots → implementation → the approved three profile builds and existing offline checks → separate bounded Attract-loop and post-game runtime acceptance → user-owned manual review of the keyboard/adaptive ROM. Exercise both High Score routes because the current build assembles different overlay variants for them. A freeze, timeout, missed rare path, failed hard limit, or missing visible Attract transition is a failure, not a pass. Keep the current hard limits unchanged.

Decision requested: approve or revise this High-risk scope amendment. The life-marker artwork question remains open; this amendment only requires gameplay state and the first-life animation to stay inactive during High Score.

2026-11-04 — Proposed amendment: root-relative Attract logo positions

Objective: Make the animated logo write to the screen cells defined by Attract's own Logo Frame 1 and Logo Frame 2 layers, while keeping one shared painter for Attract and High Score. This aligns animation with the authored Tiled frames; it does not reposition the entire logo relative to the rest of the Attract screen.

Baseline: logo_tick currently reads High Score's generated frame records for either screen. For Attract it subtracts the fixed byte offset $1E00. That moves those High Score destinations six 8-pixel rows. The retained attempt 08 records are on High Score rows 15 and 17; this arithmetic places their Attract writes on rows 9 and 11, while the corresponding current Attract frame cells include rows 7 and 9. This is a source calculation, not a measurement of the user's intended screen layout. The user has clarified that the current Tiled composition itself is also misplaced relative to the desired overall screen.

Proposed design: Give the shared painter one root destination supplied by the active screen, then store each changing tile's byte offset relative to that root. At build time, derive each screen's root from the top-left 16×16 tile root in the union of that screen's Tiled Logo Frame 1/Logo Frame 2 layers, and derive the relative offsets from the authored frame cells. The Attract and High Score screens therefore provide different roots and offset tables, while one logo_tick keeps the frame clock, draw call, and publication path. Remove the fixed $1E00 translation. A future scrolling screen could supply a root shifted by its current scroll position while reusing the same offsets; scrolling behavior, clipping, and framebuffer handling are not part of this amendment.

Alternatives: Replacing $1E00 with $2800 would fit the current map rows but remain a hard-coded translation and would become stale when Tiled moves. Duplicating the painter would duplicate timing and framebuffer-publication behavior; this proposal keeps the painter shared and makes only the screen-specific data separate.

Acceptance target: For Attract and High Score, the generated root matches each screen's Tiled frame-layer origin and every changing-cell write equals root plus the Tiled-derived relative offset; no other cell is written. High Score's existing animation remains visually unchanged. A user-owned RGB review confirms the Attract animation coincides with its authored Tiled frame cells. Moving the whole logo relative to prompts or screen borders remains a separate Tiled layout decision.

Verification and risks: The build verifier independently derives the changed frame cells and root from Tiled and confirms generated offsets, including a negative case where a moved frame cell must be rejected. This is the recurring guard against map/data drift. After implementation, freeze a fresh candidate and run the approved three distinct FEAT-010 profile builds in order, with their existing build/post-build limits and stop-on-first-failure rule. Relative destinations add a root-plus-offset operation in the painter; Attract's per-screen frame payload may also add cold data. Measure the actual code, cycle, and payload effects against the existing limits; no numeric cost is assumed. No build or runtime run is authorized by this proposal. The final RGB review remains user-owned and has no agent-imposed duration.

Disposition: Proposed, High-risk. Approval is required before implementation. The nine High Score rank-label color rules are separately approved but not build-qualified. The old attempt 08 package is stale after the color-data change and cannot qualify this amendment.

2026-11-04 — Root-relative logo alignment approved; isolated preview in progress

Decision and class: The user authorized continuing if this amendment is approved. Accept the High-risk amendment under FEAT-010. The source change affects how the shared Attract/High Score painter chooses animated tile destinations; it does not move the whole logo or alter either Tiled layout.

Confirmed layout: I read Logo Frame 1 and Logo Frame 2 from both candidate TMX maps. Each map has twelve grouped 16×16 tile roots. Their frame cells and tile IDs match at the same relative positions. The Attract root is cell (10,6), destination $3E28; High Score root is cell (10,14), destination $6628. These destinations use the renderer's $2000 + y×1280 + x×4 conversion. The eight-cell-row difference is $2800.

Approved design: Generate one table of changing-cell offsets from the shared frame root and two absolute roots from the corresponding Tiled layers. The helper caches the selected screen id and 16-bit root in three bytes of page-$23-owned storage when PRES_SCREEN changes. It selects the root once per screen, not once per tile. For each changed tile, logo_tick adds that shared root-relative offset to the cached root to form the destination; the raw draw callback clobbers registers, so the root must live in helper-owned storage. The High Score map remains the source of the shared animated frame pixels and colors. No low-RAM bytes or duplicate painter are added. A future scrolling screen can use the same relative layout only after its caller can supply a scroll-adjusted root and clipping is defined; that runtime interface and scrolling remain out of scope.

Assignment and limits: Implement only in isolated candidate repro/feat010-attract-root-20261104-03/candidate-src: scripts/build_presentation.py, scripts/verify_presentation.py, src/shared_text_stage.inc, and the logo_tick source-contract mirror/catalog records. The existing presentation verifier reads both TMX layers independently and checks their roots, shared geometry, generated offsets, and both screen destinations. Its purpose is to catch future map/data drift, not to confirm intended screen placement. Build one complete keyboard/adaptive preview with the frozen candidate command: maximum 600 seconds; then the existing static post-build flow/capacity phase: maximum 60 seconds. 2026-11-05 · proposed bounded observer — Attract selection versus A/B display buffers

Question: Determine whether one selected-menu value agrees with the selection highlight painted into each physical display buffer, and whether the visible front surface matches those buffers after publication. The ROM and runtime constraints are the same as the crash diagnosis above. Execution remains unauthorized.

Source contract: The Attract selection is MENU_SELECT at $00E0; MENU_PREV at $00DF retains input history; MENU_EVENT is at $00D0; MENU_DIRTY at $00E1 marks the two owners. FB_FRONT_ID ($008F), FB_BACK_ID ($0090), and the pending byte ($0091) identify publication state. The menu painter highlights the row matching MENU_SELECT with color 10 and paints other rows with color 7. The frozen generated records place START GAME at $6B3C (10 characters), OPTIONS at $753C (8), and CREDITS at $7F3C (8). These are screen-data destinations, not breakpoint addresses.

Bound: One RGB/GDB phase, maximum 60 seconds including launch, attach, natural input, capture, and cleanup; at most 14 target stops and 12 KiB of guest-memory reads. From the stable Attract screen, capture a baseline, then reproduce three separate controller Down presses/releases followed by three Up presses/releases. The source-derived expected selection sequence is 0, 1, 2, 2, 1, 0, 0, including the initial value and endpoint clamping.

Capture method: At each selection change, do not send the next input until both dirty-owner bits have cleared and pending is zero. Stop after menu_load_finish has painted a back buffer and before its finish/publication handoff. Record the selected value, dirty/pending state, front/back IDs, and PAR1–PAR5. Read the three menu text spans from the naturally mapped back surface, tagged with its physical owner ID. The renderer uses four bytes per cell on each of eight scanlines, with a calculated 160-byte stride between scanlines: the three spans total 832 bytes per buffer. Capture row bytes using this source-derived layout. After the normal finish, capture the visible RGB frame. During the second owner redraw, the former front is naturally the back surface, allowing its bytes to be read without remapping. Never change PAR values to reach the front surface.

Interpretation: Compare each owner’s row bytes with the sampled MENU_SELECT and the painter’s selected/unselected colors, then compare the post-publication screenshot and FB_FRONT_ID. If the selection byte changes by more than one step for one press, investigate input/menu handling. If the byte is stable but owner buffers disagree, investigate dirty tracking and repaint. If both buffers encode the same selected row but the visible frame does not, investigate publication/display selection. These are discriminators, not assumed causes. Observer completion marker: all six input transitions have the expected value trace and both physical buffer IDs are sampled for each transition, with both dirty bits clear and pending zero before the next press. If the listing cannot prove the safe stop and PAR mapping, or both owner samples cannot be obtained in the bound, stop and report incomplete rather than infer a result. A timeout is incomplete evidence, not a passing result.
